clue.text: Bread supplier on the high street?

definitions.text: Bread supplier on the high street?

blocks.clueFragment: Bread supplier on the high street?
blocks.note: surface reading: a baker's shop in a town centre
setter's reading: bread is slang for money, so this supplier dispenses banknotes from a wall

explanation.surface: A shopper looks for the local bakery among the shops of a town's main street.
explanation.walkthrough: The high street is the British main shopping street; 'bread' as money turns the baker into a machine set in a bank wall.
explanation.definitionFit: An automated teller dispenses banknotes, which slang calls bread, and such machines line every main shopping street.

clue.text: See cluer's use of rare, silly pseudo-lingo - absurd nonsense from 4

indicators.note: something absurd makes no sense, so the preceding words are thrown into a senseless new order

blocks.clueFragment: See cluer's use of rare, silly pseudo-lingo
blocks.note: the whole opening phrase, all thirty-four letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter mocks another cluer's daft made-up jargon as complete gibberish.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram gives the whole sentence, but this light keeps only its first two words: the rest runs on through 12 across, 2 down and 22 across. 4 is 4 down, the linguist who coined it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chomsky invented this sentence to show a grammatically correct string of words can still carry no meaning at all.

clue.text: See 1

blocks.note: surface reading: a pointer sending the solver to another clue
setter's reading: this light holds the fourth word of the sentence clued at 1 down

explanation.walkthrough: The 1 down anagram gives Chomsky's whole sentence; this light carries its fourth word, the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The light continues the nonsense sentence begun at 1 down, supplying the verb that its imagined thoughts perform.

clue.text: Idiotic fellow sitting on top of a tree?

blocks.note: any man's name will do for a fellow

explanation.surface: A foolish man perches up in the branches.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'sitting on top of' places the first pieces above the last.
explanation.definitionFit: The madrona is an evergreen tree of western North America, a kind of arbutus with peeling red bark.

clue.text: Linguist and Philosopher opposed to Vietnam War writing in prison

definitions.text: Linguist and Philosopher opposed to Vietnam War

indicators.note: something held in a prison is enclosed by it, so the writing sits inside

blocks.note: choky is British slang for jail
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript

explanation.surface: An anti-war intellectual is locked up and writes from his cell.
explanation.definitionFit: Noam Chomsky, the American linguist and philosopher, was a prominent campaigner against the Vietnam War.

clue.text: Like phone bill, having side organised with time?

indicators.note: to organise is to arrange afresh, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A tidy phone bill is laid out neatly with call times on one side.
explanation.definitionFit: A detailed telephone bill lists every call separately, line by line, as a set of individual entries.

clue.text: Drastic action to get readings from a maximum-minimum thermometer?

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for severe steps taken in desperation
second meaning, read literally: such a thermometer records the highest and lowest values

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense takes the idiom word by word: the readings are the most extreme values measured.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for severe remedies, and literally the highest and lowest temperatures a recording thermometer logs.

clue.text: Jail cut short as man's smuggled in tool

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter, like a sentence trimmed early
contraband smuggled into a place is hidden inside it, so one piece goes within the other

explanation.surface: A prisoner's escape tool is sneaked into his cell.
explanation.walkthrough: A down clue's jail can be a single room as well as the whole prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A chisel is a bladed hand tool for cutting wood or stone.

clue.text: Half the crew missing on the river, a desperate situation

indicators.note: only half of the following word survives, the other half dropping away
the absent half is gone from the word, confirming the loss

blocks.note: the Isis is the Thames at Oxford

explanation.surface: A rowing eight on the river loses half its oarsmen, leaving them in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isis is the name of the Thames as it flows through Oxford, a favourite crossword river. In a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a moment of acute danger or difficulty demanding urgent decisions.

clue.text: Old weapon that's iron-like, left to be buried

indicators.note: whatever is buried lies inside the ground around it, so these pieces go within another word

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An ancient iron weapon has been abandoned and interred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' doubles as the link of 'left to be' and the start of the indicator: L and BE are buried in HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A halberd is a medieval pole weapon combining an axe blade with a spike.

clue.text: Poorly-rated home kept by member of crew

indicators.note: a thing kept by someone is held within their grasp, so it sits inside

blocks.note: an oar, or oarsman, is a member of a rowing crew

explanation.surface: A rower's house gets a poor review.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotels and films given a single star in a rating scheme are judged the lowest grade.

clue.text: Lucre's somehow made with pots - but there's no ecstasy for the craftspeople

indicators.note: made somehow means made in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged freely
saying something is absent tells the solver to remove it from the letters

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Potters make money from their wares but find no thrill in the trade.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the E out of LUCRES POTS and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculptors are artists who carve or model figures, a kind of skilled craftsperson.

clue.text: See 1 down

blocks.note: surface reading: a pointer sending the solver to another clue
setter's reading: this light holds the third word of the sentence clued at 1 down

explanation.walkthrough: The 1 down anagram gives Chomsky's whole sentence; this light carries its third word, the plural noun after the two adjectives.
explanation.definitionFit: The light continues the nonsense sentence begun at 1 down, supplying the noun that the colourless green qualifiers describe.

clue.text: Endless money? Take it easy!

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: lolly is British slang for cash

explanation.surface: Someone with unlimited wealth is told to relax.
explanation.definitionFit: To loll is to lounge or sprawl lazily, relaxing without effort.

clue.text: Maiden with spare tyre trained as a successful athlete

indicators.note: training reshapes a body, so the letters are worked into a new form

blocks.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman with a paunch gets fit and becomes a sporting winner.
explanation.walkthrough: A spare tyre is a roll of belly fat. Mary Peters won pentathlon gold for Britain at the 1972 Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Peters, the Northern Irish pentathlete, was an Olympic champion and so a notably successful athlete.

clue.text: Pulsating holiday centre - Nan's knocked right out

indicators.note: one letter is knocked out of the word and the other piece takes its vacated place

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Grandma has been put to sleep by the noisy throb of a lively resort.
explanation.walkthrough: The second R of RESORT is knocked out and NAN takes its place.
explanation.definitionFit: A resonant sound is deep and reverberating, vibrating and throbbing on after it is made.

clue.text: Mind-benders making me stir around in confusion

indicators.note: stirring things around jumbles them, so these letters come out in a fresh order
being placed in a state means sitting inside it, so the jumbled letters go within

blocks.note: a mess is a confused state

explanation.surface: Hypnotists stir up a person's thoughts until they are thoroughly confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesmerists are hypnotists, who in a joking sense bend the minds of their subjects.

clue.text: Stone workers aren't stone-deaf, reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by speech, so the answer is judged by its sound

blocks.note: workers are men, and those not deaf can hear

explanation.surface: Labourers at a quarry are not completely deaf after all.
explanation.definitionFit: A menhir is a tall standing stone set upright in prehistoric times.

clue.text: Popular female given overdue boost

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A well-liked woman finally gets a long-awaited lift.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflate figures or prices is to raise them artificially, pumping them up.

clue.text: Name said to be associated with fuel chaos

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so the first word counts by its sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: a term is a name for something

explanation.surface: A shortage of petrol is blamed for disorder that someone names.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmoil is a state of great disturbance, uproar and confusion.

clue.text: What's said to restrain crawlers here?

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so the verb counts by its sound rather than spelling

explanation.surface: Something meant to stop creeping insects or babies from getting in.
explanation.walkthrough: Kerb-crawlers are men who drive slowly beside the pavement edge looking for prostitutes; the British spelling of the pavement edge is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerb-crawlers cruise along the pavement edge, so that edge is where such crawlers are found.

clue.text: Lines evident in cadaverous girl

indicators.note: lines that are evident in a face appear within it, so one piece sits inside

blocks.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway lines

explanation.surface: Wrinkles show on the face of a gaunt young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Bryony is a girl's given name, taken from a climbing hedgerow plant.

clue.text: Characters in forge naturally turned black

indicators.note: the letters wanted are characters already printed inside the phrase that follows
something turned faces the other way, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Metal in a smithy's furnace naturally goes black.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is now considered offensive; the definition reflects older usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the Spanish and Portuguese for black and was once used in English for a black person.

clue.text: See 1 down

blocks.note: surface reading: a pointer sending the solver to another clue
setter's reading: this light holds the last word of the sentence clued at 1 down

explanation.walkthrough: The 1 down anagram gives Chomsky's whole sentence; this light carries its final word, the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: The light ends the nonsense sentence begun at 1 down, supplying the adverb describing how its imagined thoughts rest.

clue.text: Chemical vent without top on at home

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed

explanation.surface: A household gas is leaking from a vent left uncovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link in a down clue, placing the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Olein is a glyceride of oleic acid, an organic compound found in fats and oils.

clue.text: In furniture store prohibit Japanese art

indicators.note: the second word is placed inside the shop's name, as goods sit in a store

explanation.surface: A shop bans a Japanese product from its shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the traditional Japanese practice of formal flower arranging.

clue.text: Storm finished? Make a dash for it!

explanation.surface: Once a tempest has passed, someone sprints for shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storm' looks like weather, but it is the verb for attacking a position.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun a place is to invade and occupy it, as troops storm a fortress.

clue.text: The girl going after catch meets boys around the north country

indicators.note: the boys stand around the compass point, enclosing it within their word

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A girl pursues a catch and meets boys in a northern land.
explanation.definitionFit: The Netherlands is a western European country, often called Holland.
